course:
The course (in general / regardless of the instructor) is an enriching course, stimulating thought in students' brains. However, more effort is put on the assignments than the content itself. Sometimes, just to gather few more points, we have to miss the essentials of the lecture and that is sometimes disturbing.

Also, the students, in general, do not participate at all. To enforce participation, maybe the weight of participation grade could be increased and some objective criteria could be put as a bare minimum.

The course should have the grading structure like this: it should be hard to pass, so that students do participate in the in-class discussions, however, it should be easy to get good grades once required amount of effort is put. On the other hand, in reality, we have the opposite. Students do prefer to pass with a C or D and that way they do not satisfy the exact requirements of the class, yet a good student needs to pay a lot of attention in order not to lose the limited amount of points.

There can be more creative parts of the courses. The syllabus is useful and even necessary to have a sense of humanity studies but we must be relaxed during these humanities. We are bored and wasted enough thanks to our own courses. So, please make humanities more relaxing!

Dersi çok iyi işliyor, konular hakkında çok bilgili ve ders yapmak ona bir yük değilmiş gibi büyük bir zevkle işliyor dersleri. Çok kibar biri, herkesin fikrine ve düşüncelerine ılımlı yaklaşıyor. Humanities gibi bir tartışma dersini bile Zoom'dan çok iyi yönetti, okunan metinlerle ilgili tahtaya not alması çok iyi oluyor sınav ve diğer assignmentlar için. Tek olumsuz denebilecek yanı bir dönem boyunca çok fazla metin okutması olabilir. Bu dönem 5 veya 6 kitap okuduk. Bu kadar fazla metin olması derste içeriklerini tartışma süremizi doğal olarak kısaltıyor ve metinleri bazen biraz çabuk geçiyoruz gibi hissettiğim zamanlar olmuştu. Ama gerçekten sadece soruda olumsuz yan sorulduğu için yazdım yoksa olumlu yanları olumsuzdan kat kat daha fazla. Bu dönem kendisinden HUM112 aldığım için çok mutluyum, teşekkürler hocam!!

This course, although well-meaning, is not designed very well. 

The 'group project' method should be eliminated and each student should be able to work on their own. Working with others compromises the student's individual grade, with them not only working twice as hard as everyone else in the group but in some cases, carrying the work load of the entire group, and still failing to achieve their full potential because of mistakes on the part of their group, for example, deadlines not being met even though one member did most of the work, and other members failed to submit their work on time. This should be corrected immediately as it is not only unfair, but extremely discouraging.

Strongest point about the course I find is that it's one of the first courses in the departments that gives us a larger academic writing task. This is important, because this is more than a gimmicky essay and it needs a lot more time and research (perhaps essays do too, but I mean the bulk of them). This is what the rest of anyone's academic life will be, so better to start early. The class is also split between group members so that we, as students, aren't bombarded with an assignment this large in large alone, yet.

Perhaps the groups may be a problem, but since we were able to coordinate well within our group, I see no reason as to complain about such a matter.

The course is also very technically, inevitably, so it does get boring at points. Nevertheless, this has to do more with us rather than the teacher and more so, the course.

- Despite being a course for "international students" it gives an overwhelming and unfair advantage to students that speak Turkish or a language similar to it. This does not lead to very good group good dynamics, since the Turkish speakers of the group have leverage over those who don't speak Turkish.  This course is one the most lopsided course I have ever taken in Bilkent.
